claims.text: TaVCrW is initially a disordered BCC solid solution.
The TaVCrW solid may exhibit short-range order and electronic excitations near the Fermi level.
An MTP trained on DFT data can replace the EAM reference potential for TaVCrW free-energy calculations.
Free energy perturbation can replace thermodynamic integration when calculating the solid-liquid Gibbs free-energy difference.
The MTP+FEP method will reduce computational cost by more than 80% relative to TOR-TILD.
The MTP+FEP free-energy result will differ from TOR-TILD by less than 0.5 meV/atom.
Achieving the stated accuracy requires the MTP to reproduce the ab initio phase-space distributions of both liquid and solid TaVCrW.
The method is applicable over a temperature range of 2000-2400 K.
A supercell containing more than 200 atoms is sufficient to resolve the relevant SRO contribution.
The MTP must reproduce configurational and vibrational entropy in the complex solid and liquid states.
Short-range order stabilizes the solid by approximately 2-3 meV/atom.
Electronic gap effects at the Fermi level materially affect the phase-space or free-energy description.
The MTP acts as a high-fidelity DFT surrogate that enables the phase-space sampling needed for FEP.
FEP based on overlap sampling or work distributions is computationally cheaper than the extensive sampling required for TI.
The MTP must achieve sub-meV/atom errors for the proposed FEP strategy to remain accurate.
Electronic excitations can shift the melting temperature by tens of kelvin.
Training the MTP on DFT data containing SRO and electronic-excitation effects prevents errors associated with underbinding or overbinding rules for V and Cr.
The predicted TaVCrW melting temperature will be within 10 K of the TOR-TILD result.
High-temperature magnetic fluctuations omitted from training may introduce free-energy errors if TaVCrW has significant magnetic moments.
NbMoTaW is a suitable simpler refractory-alloy benchmark for comparing MTP+FEP with TOR-TILD.

contradictions.description: The proposed 2-3 meV/atom SRO stabilization is attributed primarily to the solid phase, but the falsification experiment specifies measuring SRO parameters only in the liquid phase, so it does not directly validate the stated solid-state SRO contribution or its supercell-size boundary.

The mechanism says DFT-trained MTPs prevent errors associated with V/Cr functional underbinding or overbinding, whereas the uncertainty field acknowledges that those same DFT-functional issues may affect MTP accuracy. A surrogate trained on the affected DFT data would ordinarily reproduce rather than remove such systematic errors.
